newsitem.title: USA: US legislator wants quick action on ATM fee bill.
newsitem.headline: US legislator wants quick action on ATM fee bill.

text.p: The House Banking Committee should move ahead quickly on a bill to force banks to disclose controversial ATM fees imposed on non-customers, a top member of the committee said Thursday.

"I do not believe another hearing or subcommittee mark-up is necessary," Rep Marge Roukema, chairman of the Banking Committee's financial institutions subcommittee, said in a letter to Jim Leach, chairman of the full committee.
Roukema has introduced a bill to require banks to disclose to non customers using their automated teller machines (ATM) when a surcharge will be imposed.

Until last year, only a customer's bank could impose a fee for use of another bank's ATM. Both banks then shared that fee. But, beginning last April, the leading ATM networks, Cirrus and Plus, began allowing each bank to charge a fee on non-customer ATM transactions.

According to a survey released this week by U.S. Public Interest Research Group, a consumer advocacy organization, 45 percent of ATMs now impose a surcharge, up from 23 percent six months ago. The average surcharge is $1.15, the group said.
"Operators should be allowed to charge a reasonable fee to cover the cost of convenience," Roukema said.
"But ATM users need fair warning of how much is being charged before they proceed with the transaction," the New Jersey Republican added.
Roukema urged the full Banking Committee to schedule a vote on her bill.
Rep Bernie Sanders, Independent of Vermont, has introduced a bill to ban the surcharges and Senate Banking Committee chairman Alfonse D'Amato has said he will introduce a similiar measure soon.
"It is outrageous that these banks and ATM owners are charging consumers twice to access out money," Sanders said earlier this week.
"Banks are posting record profits yet they are crying poverty when it comes to ATMs," D'Amato, Republican of New York, said. "That just doesn't wash."
